issues.description: Method 'addGuestStudents' parameter type mismatch: the problem statement text (problem_statement.md) specifies addGuestStudents(String) while the UML diagram in the same problem statement and the solution implementation declare addGuestStudents(int). This conflicting parameter type (String vs int) can confuse students about the expected signature and lead to implementing the wrong method, causing compilation or test mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the problem statement text to specify addGuestStudents(int) so it matches the UML and the intended implementation. Update any examples or explanatory text that mention a String parameter to use an int parameter for the number of new guest students.

issues.description: The exercise asks for a method to add guest students but uses different parameter types across artifacts. Problem statement (problem_statement.md) explicitly requests addGuestStudents(String). The UML diagram in the problem statement and the reference implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) define addGuestStudents(int). The template file contains a TODO for addGuestStudents but does not specify a parameter type. This inconsistency can confuse students about the expected parameter type (String vs int) and lead to incorrect implementations or failing tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across all artifacts. Update the problem statement to request addGuestStudents(int) to match the UML and the solution implementation (preferred, since the parameter represents a numeric count). Alternatively, if a String parameter is intended, update the UML and solution to use addGuestStudents(String) and document how the String should be parsed into an integer.
